Hi there fellow developers :)

I'm working on a fairly ambitious project, and I keep postponing going public, because I'm worried that showing off things too early will misrepresent the game - and because I'm a little paranoid that someone will swoop in, steal the ideas, and release something similar before I do (even though the game is not really breaking any significant new ground).

I'm 6 months into the development process, with around 2000 hours spent - so there is definitely something to show, but there is a lot of incomplete systems and balance issues. Playable - but not really.

So, when do you guys/gals feel the time is right for a project to go public? What should be in place? What can be left out? What should I be prepared for?

Don't worry about people stealing ideas. I can promise you that there are hundreds of developers out there with your exact same idea. It really comes down to the implementation decisions, and you've already discovered that there are hundreds of decisions to make.

You could model your game in a spreadsheet and try to balance it there. But no matter how well you balance your game, the human players will find a way to break it. If you want to be fancy (and add a few hours of work), track what the player does and how successful it is, then upload that to a database. You can then release your game early and see how players are playing and adjust accordingly.

Yea, I'm not too worried about the whole idea stealing, when it really comes down to it. And you're right - it comes down to how those ideas are implemented.

I could write a form of telemetry, but that would be, as you wrote, for a release. I guess the 'going public' phrase was meant more as a 'when do you start releasing information, video and screenshots, without it biting you in the ass later'.

I feel that it is risky to do too early, and risky to do too late. When you've been working on a project this long, you start to question the validity of the whole thing, when no one else has seen it (or, at least no one who can give an informed opinion).

My old company released screenshots as soon as we had something visually appealing which could get people interested in the game. It was a lot of fun to interact with people commenting about the images.

Showing off your product early and interacting with potential players is something I'd recommend, and I'd highly recommend it if you need other people to join your community (like a multi-player game or a game with a level editor). Being visually appealing can mean a lot, too: video of a game mechanic working, various angles on a 3D model, or a screen capture of a GUI layout.
